title: Zuckerberg’s Yacht Booed Over Failing to Help Stranded Boat
excerpt: Meta says Mark Zuckerberg’s superyacht was using a different radio channel when a nearby skiff ran out of fuel in Alaska.
content_html:
Photo: Bloomberg/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Mark Zuckerberg and his fellow tech billionaires have a reputation for being unfeeling supervillain weirdos who, net-net, have made society a worse place than they found it. That reputation probably has to do with stuff like mistreating workers, attempting to destroy democracy, taking a jackhammer to the federal government, and causing psychological harm to children. Oh, and in the case of Zuckerberg, leaving a bunch of stranded passengers on a ship in Alaskan waters high and dry, despite the fact that his superyacht was nearby and could have helped.

Yes, the Alaska Beacon reports that Zuckerberg’s $300 million, 387-foot ship, Launchpad, did not respond to requests for assistance after a skiff ran out of fuel last week. Instead, a boat called Wilderness Legacy answered the call for help; as it did, the cruise’s captain apparently let passengers know that Zuckerberg’s boat had been closer to the stranded vessel but “refused” to spring to action, according to a report from a passenger. “There was near unanimous booing when the captain announced this,” software developer Michael Love wrote on Bluesky, adding, “Frankly, if I was Mark Zuckerberg I would be absolutely ecstatic at a chance to do something helpful for someone in need and maybe get some good PR out of it.” Per the Alaska Beacon, “Vessel tracking services in the area back up” the account, showing “the $300 million, 387-foot yacht Launchpad slowing to a halt outside Farragut Bay as the UnCruise Adventures ship Wilderness Legacy steams around and past the Launchpad, stops at the apparent site of the skiff, then tows it into sheltered Farragut Bay.”

In a statement, a spokesperson for the Meta founder said that “Mark and his family were not on board at the time of the incident,” the superyacht was using a different radio channel, and the skiff was not in distress. “By the time the crew reviewed the Coast Guard contact on a different radio channel from the one they were operating on, the assist was already underway,” the spokesperson said. “We’re grateful all parties are safe.”

While an unfortunate look, this is, of course, far from the worst thing Zuckerberg (or someone working for him) has ever been accused of by many orders of magnitude. Last week, a judge fined Meta $567 million for the psychological harm Facebook and Instagram cause children, which came on top of a $375 million civil penalty imposed by jurors in March after concluding Meta knowingly harmed the mental health of minors and covered up its knowledge of child sexual exploitation across its platforms. So the boat thing is pretty much a drop in the bucket.

A Meta spokesperson told ABC News the company would appeal the ruling and that it works “hard to keep people safe on our platforms and [has] been transparent about the challenges of identifying and removing bad actors and harmful content.”

In other Zuckerberg news, the Meta CEO published a 6,500-word defense of artificial intelligence on Monday in which he declared “it is surprising that the discourse from many developing AI is so filled with doom” — an interesting take given, among other things, the chatbots telling people how to “buy raw genetic material, turn it into deadly weapons and deploy them in public spaces.” Nevertheless, Zuckerberg says he is “optimistic that the coming decades will be some of the most amazing in history.”

content_html_zh:
照片：彭博社/彭博社，盖蒂图片社

马克·扎克伯格和他的科技亿万富翁同事以无情的超级恶棍怪人而闻名，他们让社会变得比他们发现的更糟糕。 这种声誉可能与虐待工人、试图破坏民主、拿手提钻攻击联邦政府以及对儿童造成心理伤害等事情有关。 哦，还有扎克伯格的例子，尽管他的超级游艇就在附近并且可以提供帮助，但他还是将一群滞留的乘客留在了阿拉斯加干燥水域的一艘船上。

是的，《阿拉斯加灯塔》报道称，扎克伯格价值 3 亿美元、长 387 英尺的船 Launchpad 在上周一艘小船耗尽燃料后没有回应援助请求。 相反，一艘名为“Wilderness Legacy”的船响应了求救信号。据一名乘客报告，当时，游轮船长显然让乘客知道扎克伯格的船距离搁浅船只更近，但“拒绝”立即采取行动。 软件开发人员迈克尔·洛夫（Michael Love）在 ​​Bluesky 上写道：“当船长宣布这一消息时，几乎全场响起了一致的嘘声。”他补充道，“坦白说，如果我是马克·扎克伯格，我会非常高兴有机会为有需要的人做一些事情，也许还能从中获得一些好的公关。” 据《阿拉斯加灯塔》报道，“该地区的船只跟踪服务支持”该报道，显示“价值 3 亿美元、长 387 英尺的游艇 Launchpad 在法拉格特湾外减速停下，UnCruise Adventures 的船 Wilderness Legacy 绕行并经过 Launchpad，停在小船的明显位置，然后将其拖入受庇护的法拉格特湾。”

Meta 创始人的发言人在一份声明中表示，“事件发生时马克和他的家人并不在船上”，超级游艇正在使用不同的无线电频道，小船没有遇险。 发言人表示：“当机组人员通过与他们正在操作的无线电频道不同的无线电频道查看海岸警卫队的联系时，援助已经开始。” “我们很感激各方都安全。”

虽然看起来很不幸，但这当然远非扎克伯格（或他的工作人员）曾被指控的最糟糕的事情。 上周，一名法官因 Facebook 和 Instagram 对儿童造成心理伤害而对 Meta 处以 5.67 亿美元的罚款，此前陪审员在 3 月份裁定 Meta 故意损害未成年人的心理健康并掩盖其平台上有关儿童性剥削的知识后，对 Meta 处以 3.75 亿美元的民事罚款。 所以，船的事情几乎是九牛一毛。

Meta 的一位发言人告诉美国广播公司新闻，该公司将对这一裁决提出上诉，并且“努力确保人们在我们平台上的安全，并且在识别和删除不良行为者和有害内容的挑战方面一直保持透明”。

在扎克伯格的其他新闻中，这位 Meta 首席执行官周一发表了一篇 6500 字的人工智能辩护文章，其中他宣称“令人惊讶的是，许多正在开发的人工智能的言论如此充满厄运”——这是一个有趣的观点，除其他外，聊天机器人告诉人们如何“购买原始遗传材料，将其转化为致命武器并将其部署在公共场所”。 尽管如此，扎克伯格表示，他“乐观地认为未来几十年将是历史上最令人惊奇的几十年”。
